## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈963 falls below the smallest measured point (N=4000), so its effect is invisible. At q=0.01, cost FALLS gently from 8.814 ns/p (N=4000) to a minimum of 8.164 ns/p (N=262000), then RISES modestly to 8.738 ns/p at N=4000000. The L2 spill at N≈61680 sits between N=16000 and N=65000, yet there is no knee — cost continues declining through N=65000 (8.208) and N=262000 (8.164) before the slight DRAM-regime uptick. This flat-to-declining shape across the L2→DRAM transition indicates the workload is not cache-pressure-limited. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.25 holds ~11.2–11.9 ns/p across all N, roughly 3 ns/p above q=0.01, with the same gentle rise at large N.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.33 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — only 33% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0.05 the peak drops to 7.78 GB/s (31%), and at q=0.25 to 6.06 GB/s (24%). The absence of any bandwidth knee at the L2 spill, combined with a flat ns/p curve, rules out bandwidth-bound behavior; the algorithm is compute/overhead-bound throughout. Death rate monotonically erodes achieved bandwidth by raising per-particle cost, with no regime where the algorithm approaches the ceiling.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the components of a single particle (AoS), not across particles. The inner loop loads one particle's first four floats with `ldr q7, [x10]`, rearranges them with `ext.16b v17, v7, v16, #0xc` and `mov.s v17[3], v6[0]`, then applies `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` before storing back with `str q6`. A fifth component is fetched via `ld1.s { v16 }[1], [x11]` — an indexed single-element gather from offset 0x14 — followed by `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` and `str d6`. The per-particle stride is 0x44 (68 bytes), matching bytes_per_particle. The loop2 deposit section uses `ldrb`/`strb` byte-granular scatter stores with `csel` clamping to 0xff. This component-wise AoS vectorization with an indexed gather and byte-scatter explains both the flat N-curve (each particle is self-contained, no cross-particle streaming) and the 33% ceiling: the `ld1.s` gather and `strb` writes cannot stream.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algorithm never exceeds 8.33 GB/s (33% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, N=262000, and the flat ns/p curve (8.2–8.7 across all N) shows it is compute/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Component-wise AoS vectorization with an `ld1.s` gather and `strb` byte-scatter prevents streaming, and death rate raises the floor to 11.9 ns/p (5.72 GB/s, 23%) at q=0.25 without changing the shape. Auto-vectorization over per-particle components does not approach the streaming ceiling in any regime.
